scenes.headline: The Spark Driver
scenes.subtitle: The process that plans, schedules, and coordinates every job.
scenes.narration: The driver is the central process that runs your main program and coordinates everything the application does.

scenes.headline: What the driver does
items: Runs your main() and holds the SparkSession
Converts transformations into a DAG of stages and tasks
Schedules tasks onto executors and tracks their progress
Collects final results returned by actions
scenes.narration: The driver runs your main program and holds the SparkSession. It converts your transformations into a directed acyclic graph of stages and tasks, schedules those tasks onto executors, and gathers the final results.

scenes.headline: The driver's loop
scenes.narration: The driver reads your code and builds a DAG of the work. It splits that graph into tasks, sends them to executors, and collects the results once they finish.

scenes.headline: Beware pulling data to the driver
scenes.code:
# Safe: work stays distributed
df.groupBy("user_id").count().show()

# Dangerous: collect() pulls ALL rows to the driver
rows = df.collect()  # can crash on huge data
scenes.narration: Group-by and show keep the work distributed and safe. But calling collect pulls every row back to the single driver machine, which can exhaust its memory and crash the whole application on large datasets.

scenes.text: If the driver dies, the whole application dies — protect its memory.
scenes.narration: The driver is a single point of failure, so if it dies the whole application dies. Guard its memory and avoid pulling large results back to it.
